Rover Power Distribution Board

Harvard Undergraduate Robotics Club · Fall 2025 · KiCad

Outcome. The v1 board is the fully functioning central power distribution system for the Harvard rover and operated successfully through the University Rover Challenge SAR video report and testing. It takes a 25.6 V, 50 A battery input and provides 24 V, 18 V, 12 V, 5 V, and 3.3 V output ports.

My contribution. On the power conversion side, I designed the buck converter in/out port layout, the port distribution, and the physical component layout, added fuse and capacitor protection, and provided peripheral power for fan control and the Teensy GPIO ports. On the battery management side, I designed the E-stop relay architecture and the shunt-resistor current measurement and voltage-divider monitoring, integrating both with their sensing ICs. The board was co-designed with Winfred Lin.

Skills applied. KiCad, PCB schematic design, trace calculations and layout, power distribution and protection, current and voltage sensing, MOSFET switching, mechanical integration, assembly, and bench verification.

Motivation. When I joined the team, the rover's electrical system was a row of WAGO connectors with no capacitor filtering or battery monitoring. Winfred Lin and I spent a semester designing the first comprehensive board that could adapt to each subteam's changing requirements while safely powering the rover.

Electrical Training Program & Smart Fidget Spinner

Electrical Training Lead, HURC · Fall 2025 to present · KiCad, JLCPCB

Outcome. About 15 new rover team members went from their first schematic to a fabricated board in one semester, using a smart fidget spinner PCB I designed as the teaching vehicle. The boards were fabricated at JLCPCB and assembly is the next stage. The program also produced the team's rover-wide electrical architecture schematics.

My contribution. I designed the board: a USB-C input, MCP73831 LiPo charge management, an AP2112K 3.3 V LDO, an ATtiny1614 programmed over UPDI, a LIS3DH accelerometer, and four addressable LEDs, routed on two layers around a bearing cutout. I wrote the curriculum, recorded the guide videos, and taught the sessions.

Skills applied. Mixed-signal PCB design, Li-ion charge management, LDO regulation, small-MCU firmware, I²C sensors, constrained routing, and teaching.

Motivation. New members were arriving with no hardware background and nothing to practice on. One small board that contains every subsystem a rover board needs lets them complete the full design-to-fabrication loop before they touch rover hardware.

Guide: a simple LDO regulator stageRecorded training session. Opens on YouTube.

PID Self-Balancing Robot

Hardware and firmware · Spring 2026 · ESP32-S3, MPU6050, TB6612FNG

Outcome. A two-wheeled inverted pendulum that balances and recovers from pushes on a 12 V, 2 A budget, built in two weeks for $99. It was later requested by Harvard's Area Chair for Electrical Engineering as a lab for her upper-level controls course.

My contribution. I did the circuit design, IMU characterization, final hand-soldered protoboard, and control firmware: a complementary filter (0.95 gyro / 0.05 accel), startup calibration, PID with a clamped integral and derivative dead zone, and over-the-air upload for fast tuning. After a motor driver was destroyed by an overcurrent, I added a 2 A fuse; v2 runs on LiPo with that protection. Chassis CAD was by Evie Eyers and Nicholas Bondar.

Skills applied. Sensor fusion, PID tuning, ESP32 firmware with OTA, I²C IMU configuration, H-bridge motor drive, power budgeting, and overcurrent protection.

Motivation. The inverted pendulum is the canonical unstable system. I wanted to build the full loop, sensor to actuator, on cheap hardware instead of a kit.

Watch it balanceProject video. Opens on YouTube.

Lake Monitoring Sensor Node

Sensors for Restoration · Machine Ecology seminar, Fall 2025 · EasyEDA, CNC-milled

Outcome. A single integrated node for monitoring Lake Bardawil, Egypt, with salinity, temperature, depth, and four sampling pumps on one two-layer board around a XIAO ESP32-S3 Sense. It was milled and assembled in-house and tested from bench salt baths to a full-scale tank to the lakeshore.

My contribution. I handled system integration: I consolidated every subteam's sensor and actuator onto one board, designed the schematic and layout in EasyEDA, and milled, drilled, and hand-soldered it. I also brought up the depth sensor and worked around its hardware limits in firmware. [Depth-sensor limitation and firmware approach to follow.]

Skills applied. EasyEDA, CNC PCB milling and hand assembly, 4-electrode AC conductivity sensing with thermistor compensation, UART sensors, L9110S pump drive, ESP32-S3 firmware, and field testing.

Motivation. Twelve students were selected from about 100 applicants to build an open-source tool for a real restoration project. A set of separate sensor breakouts is not deployable; one board is.

2026

Sesame quadruped power retrofit

Instead of buying the recommended distribution board, I re-architected the power electronics for an existing open quadruped design running on a 7.4 V LiPo, adding input capacitance and protection the original lacked. A quick study in picking up someone else's design and making it safer. Original design by Dorian Todd.

Follow-me ultrasonic bookbag
